The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) is a multisite longitudinal study
designed to develop clinical, imaging, genetic, and biochemical biomarkers for the early
detection and tracking of Alzheimer's disease.

Participants are classified as cognitively normal (CN), mild cognitive impairment (MCI),
or dementia at each visit. The primary diagnosis variable is stored in the DXSUM table
as DIAGNOSIS (1=CN, 2=MCI, 3=Dementia). Participant IDs use RID and PTID.

The CDR (Clinical Dementia Rating) is collected at each visit. ADNI also administers the
MMSE, ADAS-Cog, MoCA, and other neuropsychological assessments. Longitudinal MRI and
PET imaging are collected for a subset of participants. Amyloid PET and tau PET scans
follow tracer-specific acquisition protocols.
